label: Moving your body
rationale: Body instructions heard in class, at the doctor or at a massage: raise your hand, close your eyes, relax.
mixUps: Eyes take tojiru, not shimeru (which is for doors and windows). chikara o nuku pulls the strength out and is the opposite of chikara o ireru. te o ageru can also mean raising a hand to someone (hitting them).

targets.verbSense: raise, lift up; the same-sounding ageru also means give
targets.use: Heard in class, at meetings and at events as a request: shitsumon aru hito, te agete. With ni and a person it means raising a hand against them: kodomo ni te o ageru (hit a child).
targets.notes: Films inflate the count with police shouting te o agero (hands up!). Putting it down is te o orosu.

example.english: Anyone with a question, put your hand up.

examplePolite.romaji: shitsumon ga aru kata wa, te o agete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 質問がある方は、手を挙げてください。
examplePolite.english: If you have a question, please raise your hand.

targets.verbSense: close, shut (eyes, a book, an app); doors and windows take shimeru instead
targets.trap: Doors and windows take shimeru, so learners say me o shimeru. Eyes take tojiru, or the casual tsuburu: me tsubutte.
targets.use: Mostly heard as a request, me tojite: at the dentist under the lamp, with eye drops, or before a surprise. Photos are the opposite: me tsubutchatta (I blinked). Casual speech uses me tsubutte just as much, and o often drops in both.
targets.notes: Opening them again is me o akeru. Me o tsuburu also means 'let it slide' (overlook a fault).

example.romaji: ii tte iu made, me tojitete ne.
example.ja: いいって言うまで、目閉じててね。
example.english: Keep your eyes shut till I say so.

examplePolite.romaji: ii to iu made, me o tojite ite kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: いいと言うまで、目を閉じていてくださいね。
examplePolite.english: Please keep your eyes closed until I say so.

targets.verbSense: pull out, take out (a tooth, a plug); let out (air, tension); also skip (a meal)
partners: kuuki (air: let air out of a tyre)
ki (attention: ki o nuku = let your guard down)
targets.use: Heard as an instruction at massages, the doctor's, sport and yoga: chikara nuite, or motto kata no chikara nuite. O often drops in the request.
targets.notes: The opposite is chikara o ireru (put strength in). Rirakkusu shite is the other everyday instruction; chikara nuite targets a tense part (kata no chikara nuite), and kata no chikara o nuku also means 'stop trying so hard'.

example.romaji: motto chikara nuite. sou, sono kanji.
example.ja: もっと力抜いて。そう、その感じ。

examplePolite.romaji: motto chikara o nuite kudasai. hai, sono kanji desu.
examplePolite.ja: もっと力を抜いてください。はい、その感じです。
examplePolite.english: Please relax a bit more. Yes, that's it.
